case_name: C. Channabasavaiah v State of Mysore and Others
facts: These are fifty-five writ petitions under Art. 32 of the Constitution invoking Articles 14, 15 and 16 of the Constitution against the State of Mysore and the Mysore Public Service Commission in respect of appointments made to certain services in the Mysore State.

By a notification dated September 26, 1959, the Mysore Public Service Commission announced that a competitive examination would be held for direct recruitment for Class I and Class II posts relating to certain Administrative Services and numerous applicants including the petitioners offered themselves as candidates.

On September 5, 1960, the Public Service Commission modified the earlier notification and instead of holding an examination announced that the selection would be made solely on the results of a viva voce test.
issues: The legal questions or points of law being debated
petitioner_arguments: It was frankly admitted by the learned Attorney General that some of the candidates who were not selected had obtained more marks than some of those who were selected.
However, he pointed out that none of the candidates who had failed and who was a petitioner before us had obtained 56% marks or more.
respondent_arguments: The learned Attorney General attempted to show that twelve candidates were from the backward classes and four from the scheduled castes.
He contended that ninety eight candidates in the first and second selections were better than any of the petitioners and their selection could not be questioned.
court_reasoning: It appears to us, that since most of these candidates had obtained fewer marks than some of the rejected candidates it is impossible to sustain their selection.
To act otherwise opens the court itself to the charge that it did something just as bad as what was complained against.
holding: The appointment of these sixteen candidates cannot be accepted and the petitioners are entitled to claim that their marks should be compared with those obtained by the petitioners and the selection made on merit and merit alone.

With regard to the 24 candidates who were selected at the suggestion of the Government reliance is placed upon a foot note added to sub-rule (3) of r. 4 of the Mysore Public Service Commission (Functions) Rules, 1957.
cases_cited: C. Channabasavaiah v State of Mysore
